name: s42_00008.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Four Projection signs, each a flat bracket with its open side facing the center, sit just inside the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast, and west-southwest positions. Five small Crosshair signs sit about halfway between the center and the ring, at the north, east-southeast, south, west-southwest, and west-northwest positions, each rotated to face outward. The northeast stretch between the Crosshairs is slightly wider than the others, but the signs are spread evenly overall. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Projection pushes a given effect outward from the seal, so the light is cast away from it rather than held at its surface. The four Projection signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With five Crosshairs facing outward around the ring, the projected light is aimed at several separate points around the seal instead of spreading as a general glow. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Casts several modest points of light outward from the seal, each landing on a separate target around it, like small spotlights pointed in different directions. The light is soft rather than intense and gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00015.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a Link sign on the left and an earth sigil on the right. A single Columns sign sits near the ring at the west-northwest, with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. A small inverted Expansion sign, its nested corner brackets pointing inward, sits at the north-northwest. A Purification sign sits near the ring at the south. No other signs are present, and the upper-left side holds more signs than the rest of the seal.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Link shares the center and works as a second core: it identifies pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and links them. The single Columns sign gives the effect a column shape. Because it is unbalanced and sits alone at the west-northwest, the column is pushed toward that side instead of rising straight up. Expansion is semi-directional, and inverted with its corners inward it shrinks its target. Purification is asymmetric and normally separates waste from water, which fits poorly with an earth spell. The seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: linking, column direction, shrinking and purification. The earth sigil and Link dominate, with Columns setting the direction. Shrinking is secondary, and Purification is the least predictable part, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Finds fragments of stone or soil that came from the same source, links them, shrinks them and drives them in a modest column off toward the west-northwest. The shrinking acts unevenly from piece to piece, and the linked fragments sometimes shed grit and dirt in sporadic bursts. The column wavers off its line and tends to collapse before the pieces fully gather.
